title: DeJong v. Session of Village Seven Presbyterian Church
disposition_detail: The SJC denied the challenges concerning elder term limits and the Judicial Commission, sustained the challenge concerning the Governance Commission, and annulled Session’s third motion creating that commission under the adopted document.
first_summary: A ruling elder challenged Session’s proposed removal of an elder term-limit restriction and its creation of Judicial and Governance Commissions. The SJC upheld the term proposal because the Constitution is silent on terms and upheld the Judicial Commission because its assigned business was clearly defined. It sustained the Governance Commission challenge because two provisions allowed that commission to function as Session itself. The third motion was annulled, without preventing Session from adopting a constitutionally narrower plan.
summary: A ruling elder challenged Session’s elder-term proposal and its creation of Judicial and Governance Commissions. The SJC denied the first two claims: the Constitution does not regulate elder terms, and the Judicial Commission’s assigned business was sufficiently defined. It sustained the Governance Commission claim because sweeping authority and reversed delegation allowed that body to function as Session itself, contrary to BCO 15-1. Session’s third motion was annulled, but Session remained free to adopt a narrower, constitutionally compliant plan.
